primary_topics: Formal book launch of 'With Due Respect' (WDR1) published by the Philippine Daily Inquirer, March 29, 2012 -- four speakers praised the book: Ave Cruz, CJ Hilario Davide, Aurelio Montinola III (BPI President), and Washington SyCip (91 years old)

The column-writing origin: Marixi Rufino-Prieto's persistent invitation ('three times a week'); CJP's compromise ('once a week, every Sunday'); InqBooks's publication of selected 2007-2010 columns as CJP's 75th birthday gift from the Prieto family; John Nery selected the columns

The Amazon achievement: on February 11, 2012 (the 5th anniversary of his first column), Sandy Prieto-Romualdez texted that the book ranked #3 on Amazon's courts category bestseller list -- behind Jeffrey Toobin and Justice Antonin Scalia

Tribute to Isagani 'Gani' Yambot: Inquirer Publisher who wrote the WDR1 Foreword; died recently and unexpectedly; CJP pays tribute to Gani's editorial teaching and generous words in two forewords (1994's 'Love God Serve Man' and WDR1)
sub_topics: Ave Cruz tribute: ACCRA Law Chairman; close friend for 'almost half a century'; elected CJP as honorary San Beda alumnus; declined Cory Aquino's SC offer in 1986; 'I owe Ave many things, not only for his generous words today but also for the rare chance to be the chief magistrate of this country'

CJ Davide tribute: 'my esteemed predecessor as the highest magistrate'; gave CJP the opportunity 'to learn the labyrinths of that position by naming me chairman of the committee in charge of the judicial reform program'; most well-rounded government background (legislator, constitution maker, Comelec chair, UN Ambassador, CJ)
Aurelio Montinola III (BPI): 'esteemed immediate past president of the Bankers Association of the Philippines'; CJP as BPI independent director; 'rare ringside view of world-class banking'

Washington SyCip at 91: 'still robust physically and intellectually; brilliant and upright; speaks in cadenced phrases, choosing his words carefully and surely and separating the imperative from the ordinary; truly great but always humble; calls himself in his biography as Only a Bookkeeper'

Column writing origin: retired December 6, 2006; thought professional work and writing days were over; looking forward to caring for ten grandchildren; Marixi invited him 'a few days after retirement' to write a column 'three times a week'; CJP qualified himself as able to write 'only once a week, every Sunday'
75th birthday gift: last year (2011), Marixi advised InqBooks would publish selected columns as 'the Prieto family's way of celebrating my 75th birthday'; John Nery selected from 2007-2010 columns
Digital launch: made accessible in Amazon, Apple iBook Store, Apple iTunes and Barnes & Noble Nook

Amazon achievement: February 11, 2012 (5th anniversary of first column -- February 11, 2007); Sandy texted: 'my book was number three in the Amazon best seller list for the courts category, outranked only by the latest works of veteran book writer and Time correspondent Jeffrey Toobin and US Supreme Court Justice Antonin Scalia'

Gani Yambot tribute: met three decades ago when CJP was still a practising lawyer; taught him 'how to write simply but effectively by using plain English, with as little legalese as possible'; 1994 Editor's Note for 'Love God Serve Man' -- 'the book highlights the multi-faceted career... he views law not just as rigid formula but as a powerful force for giving order and justice to our society'; WDR1 Foreword: 'this is a book written by a moral man, a Christian who not only practices the forms and rituals of his faith but who also lives it'; 'I am certain he is with us, hovering above us, joining us in spirit and in truth in our celebration'

This is the most impressive external validation of his post-retirement writing career.

notable_anecdotes: The Amazon #3 text: on February 11, 2012 -- exactly the 5th anniversary of his first Inquirer column (February 11, 2007) -- Sandy Prieto-Romualdez texted that WDR1 'was number three in the Amazon best seller list for the courts category, outranked only by the latest works of veteran book writer and Time correspondent Jeffrey Toobin and US Supreme Court Justice Antonin Scalia.'

Washington SyCip at 91: 'still robust physically and intellectually; brilliant and upright; speaks in cadenced phrases, choosing his words carefully and surely and separating the imperative from the ordinary; truly great but always humble; calls himself in his biography as Only a Bookkeeper.' -- the most vivid portrait of an nonagenarian in the corpus.

Gani Yambot's ghostly presence: 'Were it not for his untimely demise, I am sure Gani would have been with us in person today. And even as I say this, I am also certain he is with us, hovering above us, joining us in spirit and in truth in our celebration.' -- the most poignant close in this batch.

The column compromise: Marixi wanted three columns a week; CJP: 'Having retired from active writing and looking forward to a more relaxed load after continuously working since I was ten years old, I thought I was qualified to write only once a week, that is, every Sunday.'

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered March 29, 2012 at the formal launch of 'With Due Respect' (WDR1) published by the Philippine Daily Inquirer, this address by CJP thanks four speakers: Ave Cruz (ACCRA Law Chairman; close friend for half a century; declined Cory Aquino's SC offer in 1986 -- 'there would have been no Chief Justice Hilario G. Davide Jr. and Chief Justice Artemio V. Panganiban'); CJ Hilario Davide (predecessor; gave CJP the APJR committee chairmanship; 'most well-rounded government background' of any jurist); Aurelio Montinola III (BPI President; past Bankers Association president; CJP as BPI independent director); and Washington SyCip (91 years old; 'still robust physically and intellectually; speaks in cadenced phrases, choosing his words carefully; truly great but always humble; calls himself in his biography as Only a Bookkeeper'). He narrates the column origin: Marixi Rufino-Prieto invited him 'a few days after retirement' to write three columns a week; CJP compromised on once-weekly; 'having continuously worked since I was ten years old, I thought I was qualified to write only once a week, every Sunday.' Last year (2011), Marixi advised InqBooks would publish his selected 2007-2010 columns (chosen by John Nery) as the Prieto family's 75th birthday gift; it was made available digitally on Amazon, Apple iBook Store, iTunes and Barnes & Noble Nook. On February 11, 2012 -- exactly the 5th anniversary of his first column (February 11, 2007) -- Sandy Prieto-Romualdez texted that the book ranked #3 on Amazon's courts category, 'outranked only by the latest works of Jeffrey Toobin and US Supreme Court Justice Antonin Scalia.' He closes with a tribute to Inquirer Publisher Isagani 'Gani' Yambot, who wrote the WDR1 Foreword but recently died unexpectedly: Gani taught CJP 'how to write simply but effectively by using plain English, with as little legalese as possible'; his WDR1 Foreword described it as 'a book written by a moral man, a Christian who not only practices the forms and rituals of his faith but who also lives it.' CJP: 'I am certain he is with us, hovering above us, joining us in spirit and in truth in our celebration.'
